findings.claim: Contractless mode inverts the field rule. `IsPublicReadWrite` accepts a field only when `field.IsReadOnly` is true. As a result, ordinary public mutable fields of T are silently left out of the generated formatter, which loses their data. Public `readonly` fields are selected as writable, so the generated deserializer assigns to a readonly field and the user's project gets CS0191. The requirement asks for contractless behaviour over public members. Surrogate mode inherits the same bug: a surrogate member that names a mutable field gets a spurious MsgPack022.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterRequirementGapTests.PublicMutableFieldOfReferencedTypeIsSerialized. It fails on head because the generated source never mentions `DistinctiveField`. Mutation receipt: change `field.IsReadOnly` to `!field.IsReadOnly`; that test then passes.

findings.claim: An acceptance criterion is not met: MessagePack attributes on T are never honoured. `Collect` always uses `CreateContractlessMembers(type)` when no surrogate is given and never looks at `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key]`, `[IgnoreMember]` or `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]` on T. A referenced type whose `[IgnoreMember]` member is meant to stay off the wire therefore gets that member serialized under a string key. Its `[Key(n)]` integer layout is replaced by a map, which produces bytes that are incompatible with the dynamic resolver. The criterion says 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured', and the maintainer note says to go contractless only when there is no `[DataContract]`/`[MessagePackObject]`.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterRequirementGapTests.MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedTypeAreHonoured. On head the generated formatter still references `DistinctiveSecret`, which is marked `[IgnoreMember]` on T.

findings.claim: 'Contractless behaviour over public members' is implemented more narrowly than MessagePack's existing contractless mode. Get-only public properties are dropped from serialization. Types that only have a parameterized constructor are rejected with MsgPack007, because `constructorParameters` is always empty. Immutable library types, a common shape for dependency-free Project A types, therefore cannot be formatted at all.

receipt_plan.detail: Read GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect, lines 77-81 (the parameterless-constructor requirement) and the `IsPublicReadWrite` filter in CreateContractlessMembers. Compare these with ContractlessStandardResolver, which serializes get-only properties and matches constructor parameters.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Key control comes from a separate surrogate type, which is what the change implements. `GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute` exposes a public `Type? SurrogateType` property. Without a surrogate, T is serialized contractless (string keys from public read-write members). With a surrogate, its `[Key]`/`[IgnoreMember]` attributes are matched to T's members by name (`CreateSurrogateMembers`, MsgPack022). Attributes on T itself are not consulted.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Key control comes from attributes on T itself, using the issue's alternative (1) and the maintainer's 'if there are attributes, we'll use them'. Remove `SurrogateType`, `CreateSurrogateMembers` and MsgPack022. In `GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect`, check T for `[MessagePackObject]` (honouring `[Key]`/`[IgnoreMember]`, int or string keys) or `[DataContract]` (honouring `[DataMember(Order/Name)]`/`[IgnoreDataMember]`, which System.Runtime.Serialization provides with no dependency) and build members from those. Use contractless string-key members only when neither attribute is present.
